subject: Implementation & cost/performance tuning plan for FluxPay (batching/caching/quant)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation & cost/performance tuning plan for FluxPay (batching/caching/quant)

Sarah — great to connect last week. Per our discovery call, FluxPay's two primary objectives for the POC are: (1) hold tail latency under 300ms p95 for user-facing flows, and (2) reduce per-1k-token inference cost by ~30% compared to your current managed setup.

To get the implementation started I sketched a short, pragmatic plan focused on cost/performance tuning during onboarding. The attachments include a compact checklist (MAPS-implementation-checklist-v1.pdf) and our recommended benchmark template (fluxpay-benchmark-results.csv). High level: 

- Day 0 (this week): confirm traffic profile (seq lengths, burst patterns, avg requests/min), and whether model will stay hosted or require private deployment.
- Week 1: baseline benchmarks (unbatched) + KV/prefix caching candidate prompts.
- Week 2: quant profile sweep + batching policy experiments (latency-first and cost-first configs).
- Week 3: routing policy test (on-cost vs latency routing) and final recommended config for production.

As a first ask: can you share a 24-48h sample of request logs (anonymized) and a preferred window for a 60-min calibration call? Also flag any hard constraints (e.g., air-gapped requirements, max acceptable mem footprint for quantized models).

I'll loop in Aisha (CS lead) and Priyom (runtime engineer) to own the implementation steps. We aim to deliver a recommended config with measured tradeoffs and a short runbook for your SREs.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Implementation & cost/performance tuning plan for FluxPay (batching/caching/quant)

Thanks, Rishi — that plan looks reasonable. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our typical user flow has median seq length ~140 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens. Peak RPS is ~85 for the payments UI during batch settlement.
- We will be on a VPC private deployment (can't send raw logs off-prem). We can provide an anonymized sample and a redacted histogram instead of full logs.
- Quantization: our security team is wary of very aggressive 4-bit profiles unless you can point to prior customer results.
- Can you confirm what you mean by "routing policy"? We have two regions (us-west/us-east); prefer routing by latency but are open to a cost-tier for non-critical batch jobs.

Available windows for calibration call: Thu 18 Mar 10–11am PT or Mon 22 Mar 2–3pm PT.

Appreciate the attachments — I'll have our DevOps pull the sample and the histogram.

—Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FluxPay
sarah.chen@fluxpay.com

Subject: Re: Implementation & cost/performance tuning plan for FluxPay (batching/caching/quant)

Sarah — thanks for the details. Breaking down an actionable onboarding checklist below (short, with owners and acceptance criteria). I'll lead the work and Priyom will run the kernel/quant experiments.

1) Data & sampling (owner: FluxPay / DevOps):
   - Deliver: 48h anonymized request sampler + histogram (seq length, tokens per request, timestamped RPS). Acceptance: file uploaded to our secure Drive link.

2) Baseline run (owner: Redwood / Priyom):
   - Run the unbatched baseline on the proposed model variant in your VPC. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU mem. Acceptance: measured p95 < 600ms for baseline.

3) Caching candidates (owner: Redwood):
   - Identify stable prefixes for KV caching and run prefix-hit simulations. Acceptance: candidate set that yields >=12% token reduction in simulation for payments UI flows.

4) Batching policy experiments (owner: Redwood):
   - Two configs: latency-first (max batch size 8, low wait) and cost-first (max batch size 32, 40ms wait). Acceptance: documented tradeoff curve (latency vs cost) with recommended default.

5) Quant sweep (owner: Priyom):
   - Run quant profiles (16->8->4-bit) on a trimmed model variant: measure accuracy drift (BLEU/QA exact-match on our eval set) and mem/CUDA allocations. Acceptance: choose lowest-bit profile with <=3% quality regression and stable mem footprint.

6) Routing policy (owner: Rishi):
   - Suggest policy: region-latency primary; for background settlement jobs route to cost-tier (dedicated spot pools) with fallback to low-latency pool on failures. Acceptance: runbook + automated fallback rule in Console.

7) Final run and handoff (owner: FluxPay + Redwood):
   - Run 24h with recommended config, collect cost per 1k tokens and SLO metrics. Acceptance: p95 under 300ms and >=28% cost reduction vs baseline.

Notes/constraints: we will not run 4-bit profiles until FluxPay signs off; priors show 8-bit LLM quant is a good starting tradeoff. I've attached a short test matrix (MAPS checklist) you can use to sign off each step.

Proposed schedule: Thu 18 Mar — calibration call (30–60m). Week of Mar 22 — baseline + experiments. Week of Mar 29 — final config and handoff.

Please confirm Thu 18 Mar 10:00am PT and we'll send the calendar invite with a secure upload link for the sampler.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success Lead — Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.ai

Subject: Internal: FluxPay onboarding responsibilities + quick notes

Internal — quick summary for the team before calibration call next week. Keeping this short: 

- Aisha: lead CS engagement and acceptance criteria. Primary POC contact.
- Priyom: run kernel selection + quant sweep in FluxPay VPC image; start with 8-bit variants and collect accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
- Stephanie: prepare Console routing rules templates (region-latency and cost-tier fallback) and the runbook snippets for SRE handoff.
- Me: coordinate scheduling, pricing impact summary, and will own final signoff with FluxPay.

Key technical risks to watch: 
- VPC access model may limit us from streaming raw sampling; ensure secure upload link is compatible with FluxPay's firewall.
- If prefix diversity is high, caching gains may be limited; plan for more aggressive batching configs in that case.

Action items for Priyom: pre-warm the quant test harness and bring a small toy dataset so we can iterate quickly during week-of Mar 22.

I'll send the calibration invite for Thu 18 Mar 10:00am PT to Sarah and their DevOps.

—Rishi
